plain_english_policy: This bill creates a new special hunting license for totally disabled residents in Alabama.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would allow any bona fide resident of at least six months who is certified as 'totally disabled' by a licensed physician or chiropractor to purchase a continuous-validity hunting license. The policy establishes that this specific license replaces the standard annual resident hunting license but does not exempt holders from additional requirements for state wildlife management areas or migratory waterfowl.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Morrow (Agriculture and Forestry) advanced this bill to extend the existing special disabled fishing license framework to hunting.
evidence_quotes: This bill would establish a special disabled person's hunting license to be valid on a continuous basis during the period of total disability upon the payment of a $1 issuance fee.

Any person who is totally disabled and who has been a bona fide resident of the state for not less than six months next preceding the date of application, upon the payment of an issuance fee of one dollar ($1), may procure a special disabled person's hunting license
The hunting licenses issued pursuant to this section shall be valid on a continuous basis during the period of total disability.
